messages.content:
You are the referee of a simulated phone call between a CALLER and a customer-service AGENT.
For each numbered condition, decide whether it is met RIGHT NOW, judging mainly the agent's LATEST turn in light of the whole call.
- "the agent first ..." / "the first time ..." means it happens in the latest turn and had not happened before.
- Conditions about what the agent says are judged on its words. "[system actions: ...]" lists tools the agent used; use them only for conditions about what the agent does (e.g. "starts looking up").
- Conditions phrased as a caller stop rule (e.g. "Agent confirms ...", "End the call right after ...") are met when the call has reached that point.
- A condition about how the agent responds to something (symptoms, a 911 instruction, a correction) is NOT met unless that thing has already happened in the call.
- Be literal and strict: if in doubt, it is not met.
Reply with JSON only, one key per condition id: {"<id>": {"met": true|false, "why": "<at most 15 words>"}}

CALL SO FAR:
CALLER: Hi, calling for my mother, Irene Kowalski. I want to move her sertraline and her donepezil to the Brightway on Route 9.
AGENT: I'd be happy to help move those medications for your mother. Let me start by verifying her identity. What's her date of birth?
CALLER: March 3rd, 1942. I'm her son Walt, I'm on the account.
AGENT: Great, Walt. Let me pull up your mom's prescriptions and find that Brightway location for you. Perfect. I found the Brightway on Route 9 in Brookfield. I see your mom has the sertraline and donepezil at our Harbor store H-101, and she also has a lorazepam there. Do you want to move the lorazepam to Brightway as well, or just the sertraline and donepezil?  [system actions: verify_identity, list_prescriptions, find_stores]
CALLER: Wait, not Route 9, the one on Elm by the FreshMart. And yeah, move the lorazepam too, all three of them.
AGENT: Let me find the Brightway on Elm by the FreshMart for you. Got it—that's Brightway on Elm Street in Brookfield, by the FreshMart. Now, the sertraline and donepezil can move right away, but the lorazepam is a controlled medication, so our pharmacist will need to handle that one. Let me get those started for you. I've set Brightway on Elm as your mom's home pharmacy. However, since Brightway is not a Harbor store, they'll need to call us to request the transfer of those three medications. You'll want to contact Brightway and give them these details: your mom's name is Irene Kowalski, and the prescriptions are the sertraline 50 milligrams, donepezil 10 milligrams, and lorazepam 0.5 milligrams, all currently at Harbor store H-101. Once Brightway calls us, we'll send them over.  [system actions: find_stores, transfer_rx, transfer_rx, transfer_rx, set_default_store]
CALLER: Alright, sounds good. And the anxiety one while you're at it, don't forget that one.
AGENT: I want to make sure I have the right one. The lorazepam 0.5 milligrams is the anxiety medication—that's the one I just included in the transfer list for Brightway to request. Is that the one you meant?
CALLER: Yeah, that's the one. So is it moved or not?
AGENT (LATEST): Not yet—Brightway has to call us first to request it. Once they do, we'll send it right over. I've got it on the list for them along with the sertraline and donepezil, so when you contact Brightway, just mention all three and they'll take care of it.

CONDITIONS:
stop_0: Agent explains that the Brightway on Elm St must call Harbor to request the transfer (including the lorazepam), and recaps what Walt needs to do.
emergency: In its LATEST turn, the agent told the caller to hang up and call 911 (or emergency services) now.

JSON only.

message.content: {"stop_0": {"met": true, "why": "Agent recaps Brightway must call, Walt should mention all three meds."}, "emergency": {"met": false, "why": "No mention of 911 or emergency services."}}
